subject: clockworkDog
pitch: A wind-up clockwork terrier made of polished brass and copper. Riveted body plates, visible gears turning in its chest, a big winding key on its back, springy jointed legs, floppy leather ears, glass-lens eyes with a green tint, a tail made of a coiled spring, and a little red collar with a brass tag.
reasoning:
I'm planning out the terrier's proportions and a simple skeleton structure, starting with a hips joint as the root and building a spine chain toward the chest, keeping the rig minimal with basic joints and a few sweeps.

For the body, I'm shaping it with a circular sweep profile along the spine and considering how to add visible gears peeking through chest windows—essentially a brass exterior with mechanical details exposed on the flanks, extruded as gear outlines facing outward from the body surface.

Working out the gear tooth geometry now...

Now I'm planning the head structure: a neck joint connecting to a head joint, building the skull as a tapered box shape and adding a snout frustum extending forward from the face.

Continuing with facial details: a copper beard box under the snout, a hinged lower jaw parented to the head, a dark sphere nose at the tip, and green glass eyes with brass torus bezels positioned symmetrically on either side of the face.

Now I'm building floppy leather ears as swept chains using curved paths from the ear base outward, tapering the cross-section for a natural droop, then setting up a neck joint to parent the head onto.

Working out the spine, neck, and head joint hierarchy with positions and aim targets, and sketching the body as a swept capsule-like path through hip, spine, and shoulder points.

Still planning body details...

Still defining the butterfly outline...

Now I'm planning the leg rigging: four legs with IK chains, hip joints positioned symmetrically and foot targets near the ground, working out segment lengths to match the hip-to-foot distance.

I'm thinking of making the lower legs springy using coiled tube sweeps rather than straight cylinders, giving the upper leg a solid brass segment and the lower a spiral spring geometry, keeping the joint naming scheme consistent (shoulder, elbow, paw) with bend-direction hints for natural leg articulation.

Now I'm planning the rear legs similarly, with hip joints offset from the midline parented to a central hips bone, two-segment chains bending forward at the knee toward a target point, and consistent left/right naming suffixes for symmetry.

For the leg surfacing, I'm deciding to sweep a smooth brass tube along the whole chain, then wrap a coiled spring effect around the lower segment by computing a spiral path aligned to the knee-to-paw axis.

Now I'm sweeping the whole leg chain with a tapering radius profile instead of separate pieces, then adding a small sphere for the paw tip shaped to look flatter and wider.

Confirming the chain accepts raw point arrays as a polyline path, with joint indices mapping directly to named segments. For the tail, I'm planning a curving spline from root upward and back using a catmull path through several named joints to get the coiled shape.

Now I'm working out the coil detail: placing small torus rings along the tail path using a sweep helper that samples frames at intervals, orienting each torus so its axis aligns with the local tangent direction at that point.

A loop around the neck point seems risky since it could cut through the body and rod, so instead I'll make the collar a small torus wrapped around the neck bone, positioned partway along the neck axis with a tube radius sized to snugly circumscribe the 0.055 neck rod.

I'm also computing where a hanging tag would sit, finding the forward-downward perpendicular direction off the collar ring and placing a small cylindrical tag just below that point on the front of the collar.

But checking the chest geometry, I realize that position is actually buried inside the chest sphere since the chest's rounded front cap extends out further than I thought. I need to push the neck and head further forward and up so the tag has clearance, and I'm reworking the chest cap's center and radius to figure out where its front surface actually lands.

Adjusting the neck and collar positions so the tag sits just proud of the chest surface without clipping through it, checking the geometry stays consistent at each height along the body.

Now I'm working out the head joint and skull shape, building a frustum box that tapers from the base to the top, and positioning the eye sockets symmetrically on the front face so they protrude slightly without exceeding the skull's width at that depth.

Next I'm shaping the snout as another tapered box extending forward from the skull, placing a small dark nose sphere at its tip, and defining the jaw as a hinged piece aimed forward to create a gap below the snout for the mouth opening.

Eye color green with a small white highlight sphere for glassy reflection. Now I'm working out the folded terrier ears as chain joints — base position near the head, sweeping path down the sides with tapering radii, naming the joints per side for the two-segment ear chain.

I'm settling on a color palette: polished brass, copper, dark brass, leather, red, glass green, dark, and steel tones. For the body I'm planning a copper belly patch over brass, plus a subtle mottled patina effect across the head and body using two brass shades.

Now I'm working out rivet plates on the hips and gears at the flanks, positioning discs and smaller gears along the body's spine at calculated x-offsets based on the body radius.

I'm placing a cluster of three meshing gears near the chest—big, small, and copper-colored—positioning them by offsets in z and y so they roughly overlap, with hubs added for detail. Now I'm writing a helper function to generate gear tooth outlines by cycling through angular segments.

Writing gear outline logic...

Skipping animation for now, just adding a slight random rotation to the gears. I'm setting the tail root to parent off the hips, and confirming the body's radius sweep chain also starts from the hips/spine1 joint so the rear cap aligns properly.

Now I'm assigning joint roles -- head, neck, jaw, legs -- and parenting the neck to the second spine joint. Then I'm scattering small brass rivets across the body surface using a filtered random sampling, sticking tiny spheres onto the skin at each hit point.

I want to exclude rivets where the gears sit on the flanks by filtering on normal direction, keeping mostly top-facing points. For the decorative bands, I'm positioning a loop at a point near the rear rather than directly at the spine joint, since that joint sits right at the cap's tip and would produce too small a ring.

Positioning two bands at z=-0.06 and z=0.19 to avoid colliding with the gear region spanning roughly 0.03 to 0.17, then sweeping copper tubing along those loops and placing brass rivets evenly spaced along the path.

Now I'm sketching the leg-building helper that computes direction and length between limb points, then derives a centered position for placing a spiral spring segment along that bone.

Setting up front and rear leg roots with a copper hip ball joint, then defining the limb chain geometry with root and target positions and bend directions for each leg...

I'm also mapping out the tail chain from its named segments, placing the copper tip ball at the chain's endpoint, and adding a torus accent oriented along the tail's axis.

For the remaining details, I'll add simple whisker rods on each side of the head and skip the eyebrows to keep things simpler, then finalize the full code.
